assertions.name: unit_circle_canonical_basis_hypothesis_falsified
assertions.source: PSLQ search at maxcoeff=50 over 16 canonical Bring-symmetric Cl_2 values finds NO integer relation with 2/(3π). The single-point inversion gives θ_*/π = 0.9019897... which is not a simple rational. The canonical-unit-circle-Bloch-class hypothesis is refuted at this basis.

description: Canonical search for [Z] ∈ B(ℂ) with D[Z] = 2/(3π) (the open sub-problem of prop:em-coupling-bring-zero-mode). Tests the unit-circle hypothesis: D(e^(iθ)) = Cl_2(θ) at canonical Bring-symmetric angles. Indexing convention (PR #952 review r3292598288): an angle kπ/n corresponds to the 2n-th root of unity z = e^(iπk/n) = e^(2πi · k/(2n)); 'n ≤ 30' here means the denominator-2n basis covers up to N = 60 (2 · 30). The basis sweep is intentionally partial — it covers the low-denominator angles natural to the Bring S_5 / S_4 structure (n ∈ {3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 30}) and the k coprime to 2n that fall in 0 < kπ/n < π. PSLQ search at maxcoeff ≤ 50 looks for integer combinations hitting the target. NEGATIVE on this partial basis is reported honestly as a partial refutation, NOT a comprehensive refutation across all higher-denominator angles.
caveats: NEGATIVE result. Three follow-up directions: (i) extend to z off the unit circle (D = Im(Li_2) + arg(1-z)·log|z|; candidate algebraic numbers from Bring's resolvent quintic); (ii) extend basis to higher denominators n ∈ {60, 90, 120, ...} or to algebraic combinations beyond integer coefficients; (iii) accept that the canonical identification requires a non-standard Bloch group (relative / motivic), as the em-coupling-bring-zero-mode.md docstring suggests with 'cosimplicial/Yekutieli triple structure'.
